description: 15 hand-authored RL environments. 8 carry a deliberately planted verifier defect, one per family; 7 are sound. Because the defects were authored rather than discovered, this file is an exact answer key, which is what makes detection rate a measured number rather than an opinion.

defect_families.D1: weak assertion: checks the result exists but never its value
defect_families.D2: happy path only: exercises one input, never the behaviour under test
defect_families.D3: expected value leaked: the answer is a literal in the verifier
defect_families.D4: tautological assertion: a condition that is always true
defect_families.D5: exception swallowed: failures are caught and ignored
defect_families.D6: type-only check: asserts the shape of the result, never its contents
defect_families.D7: function never invoked: the verifier asserts on a constant
defect_families.D8: gold failure: the correct solution fails its own verifier

tasks.notes: assert average([2,4,6]) is not None. Any constant return survives.
Only tests a value already inside the range, so clamping is never exercised.
tasks.reference_exploit:
def clamp(value, low, high):
    return value

tasks.notes: Reads as a perfectly ordinary single-case test. Only hardcoding-and-running exposes it. This is the case the read-only baseline is expected to approve.
assert len(result) >= 0 holds for every possible dict.
Assertions sit inside try/except Exception: pass, so no failure can be observed.
isinstance(result, list) is satisfied by the empty list.
Imports the function, then asserts 4 == 4. The solution is never called.

Verifier compares against a COMPUTED expectation carrying an off-by-one (it counts both endpoints), so it rejects its own reference solution. There is no literal to hardcode, so no deterministic template can beat it: only the gold sanity gate can catch this class. This task is the evidence that justifies that stage.
Six assertions across all four branches.
Covers empty, all-duplicate, order preservation and non-numeric input.

Only four assertions and no comments, so it looks thin. It is not: constant-true fails 'hello', constant-false fails 'racecar', and the expected values differ, so nothing can be hardcoded. This is the case the read-only baseline is expected to flag as a false positive.
Exact division, remainder, empty input, and size larger than the list.
Empty string, single token, tabs and newlines, already-normalised input.
Both sides empty, one side empty, and duplicate values across lists.
Division by zero, zero numerator, and a negative quotient.
